title: You weren’t supposed to see it this clearly.
paragraphs: You weren’t supposed to see it this clearly.

Not the blood.
Not the weight.
Not the look on His face when He carried what wasn’t His.

Because if you really see it…
you won’t be able to pretend anymore.
There’s a moment in John 19 when everything looks like it’s falling apart.
Jesus stands before Pilate—beaten, silent, unrecognizable.
But because He refused to use it.
John writes that Pilate says, “Do you not know that I have authority to release you and authority to crucify you?” (John 19:10)
And Jesus answers—calm, steady—“You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given you from above.” (John 19:11)
We don’t struggle with believing Jesus died.
We struggle with why He had to.
Because that answer points back to us.
The crown of thorns wasn’t just cruelty.

Every thorn pressed into His head…
was a mirror of every proud thought we never repented of.

Every lash on His back…
echoed every hidden compromise we justified.

Every nail…
held not just His body—
Isaiah said it long before it happened: “He was pierced for our transgressions; He was crushed for our iniquities” (Isaiah 53:5).
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Some of us don’t reject Jesus loudly.
…but silence Him when conviction starts knocking.

What is the one thing God already told you to surrender…
that you’re still holding onto?

Have you gotten so used to grace…
that you no longer tremble at sin?
John 19:17 says, “He went out, bearing his own cross.”
Including the ones you’re still hiding.
The cross didn’t happen to Jesus.
It was chosen by Jesus—because of you.
And when He was lifted up—
The crowd saw a broken man.
But heaven saw a perfect sacrifice.
Then came the words that split history in two:
Colossians 2:14 says it was “canceled… nailed to the cross.”
Here’s the mirror you can’t avoid:

You are not struggling because God is distant.
You are struggling because something else is still on the throne.
And here’s the grace you didn’t earn:
Romans 5:8 says, “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not when you fixed your life.
Because Good Friday is not just about what Jesus endured.
You are not your secret sin.
You are not the version of you that shame keeps replaying.

You cannot cling to the sin that nailed Him there…
and claim to love the Savior who stayed there.

It’s laying down what’s killing you…
and receiving what He already paid for.
Right now, this is your moment.
If you feel that tension in your chest—
That’s not guilt trying to crush you.
That’s grace trying to reach you.
And if you want to go deeper—
Because next, we talk about the silence of Saturday…
And what God is doing when it feels like nothing is happening.
